function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** such as β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels**: voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav), ligand‑gated NMDA receptor
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases**: EGFR, HER2
• **Integrins** (αβ heterodimers, e.g., α5β1)
• **Cadherins** (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels, e.g., Cx43)
• **Tetraspanins** (CD9, CD63) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions; often link to cytoskeleton or signaling complexes. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to spectrin)
• **Spectrin** (cytoskeletal scaffold)
• **Actin‑binding proteins**: ezrin, radixin, moesin (ERM family)
• **Src family kinases** (e.g., Src, Fyn) – attach via lipid modifications
• **Glycophorin A** (hemoglobin‑binding protein in erythrocytes)
• **Mucin‑1** (glycoprotein with a large extracellular domain) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to membrane lipids (e.g., farnesyl, geranylgeranyl, palmitoyl). | • **H-Ras** (farnesylated)
• **K-Ras** (farnesylated)
• **N‑myristoylated Src** (palmitoylated) | | **Glycoproteins & glycolipids** | Often part of the extracellular matrix or cell‑surface recognition. | • **MHC class I & II molecules** (antigen presentation)
• **Selectins** (cell adhesion)
• **Neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM)** | ### How to explore more - **Databases**: UniProt, Human Protein Atlas, and the Protein Data Bank list membrane proteins with subcellular localization annotations. - **Functional categories**: Ion transporters, receptors, adhesion molecules, enzymes, and structural proteins all contribute to the diverse roles of the plasma membrane. Feel free to ask if you’d like a deeper dive into any particular class or specific proteins!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like actin-binding proteins, ankyrin, spectrin.
